newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate edge up on liquidity squeeze.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate edge up on liquidity squeeze.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates inched up 10 basis points to 21.50 percent in early trade on Thursday amid what traders said was tight liquidity on demand for cash prior to the forthcoming long weekend.
"Rates look like they'll be under some pressure, as there's a long weekend and then it's Easter week," a trader said.
Mexican financial markets will close on Friday, March 21, to honor 19th-century President and national hero Benito Juarez.
Overnight rates on bank paper were meanwhile unchanged at 23.10 percent.
Another trader foresaw a speculative session ahead of Easter week.
"Many companies want to invest in the money market from today onwards, ahead of next week, so those who have cash can speculate," a trader said.

Dealers said secondary rates were also under pressure from the peso, which was soft following an early increase in U.S. long bond rates on hints by Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan that the Fed could raise rates as early as next week.
Benchmark 48-hour rates were 0.4 of a centavo weaker in early trade, at 7.9400/7.9440 per dollar.
U.S. 30-year Treasury bonds were down 4/32 to yield 7.00 percent.
Dealers said overnight Cetes rates could climb to 22.50 percent during the session on pressure from the U.S. bond market in the wake of Greenspan's testimony to a U.S. Congress panel.
Total liquidity of 9.454 billion pesos was slated to return to the system from previous central bank participation, traders said.
Thursday also sees the central bank place government securities it auctioned on Tuesday night, but total maturities exceed new issues by 784 million pesos and will thus cut into market liquidity.
Dealers said corporations would also pay tax bills estimated at nine billion pesos, which would squeeze liquidity further.
